findings.reason: the author must either exempt `_insert_authored_section` and the two contract readers by site (and widen the rule's enumerated forms to match, since a rule blind to `select_one` and string heading finds would pass with a second walk alive — the exact undercount the section says it exists to prevent) or narrow the "nothing in `_store.py`" done-when, and one of those is required before the §17 gate can pass.
findings.text: `_insert_authored_section` calls `body_soup.find("h2")` (817) to reject a nested heading and spells an inline `]*>` regex beside `_SECTION_OPEN_RE` (825); the section-contract readers call `find_all("h2", id=True)` on synthesized fragments (`_require_section_contract` at 1791 and `_require_new_section_contracts` at 1817/1820). None of these is among the thirteen names §17 moves to `_plan_html.py` and none is listed as an exemption, yet §17 states "every heading walk in the package is rewritten to call the reader" and its done-when demands the heading-walk rule report nothing in `_store.py`. Two of these (817, 819/825) walk a caller-supplied body fragment rather than the plan document, and two (1791, 1817/1820) walk a synthesized before/after HTML, so they cannot call a document-level `plan_headings` — they are structural-validity checks, not section locators — but the design names neither the exemption nor the rewrite for them. It also shows the rule's method list is under-specified: it enumerates `find_all`, `find` and `select`, while the tree additionally uses `select_one` and string `html_text.find("")` (925, 955) forms the rule does not name.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the complexity lands behind one private `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` projected by `plan_headings`, one module-private `_section_digests`, and one coverage predicate that is a join over the existing `list_plan_reviews` and the outstanding-sections reader rather than a new walk.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/_store.py` retains heading walks the §17 design does not name among its thirteen moved helpers or its exemptions, so its done-when requiring the heading-walk rule to report "nothing in `reckon/_store.py`" cannot hold.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names one added public definition (`strip_tags`), §17 two (`plan_headings` plus the machinery predicate) with `landed_section_ids` a re-homed same-name move, and §18 one (the classification predicate), each stating in its own text why nothing can be retired; no section adds to cli_options, mcp_views or refusal_families (§16 explicitly reuses the plan-review-missing family).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design (§16–§18) cites the existing machinery it extends, and its own censuses reproduce exactly at the head I measured: `grep -rn '"data-reckon"' reckon/` = 14 lines across 5 files (`_plan_html.py` 4, `_store.py` 3, `mcp_views.py` 5, `plan_review.py` 1, `doccheck.py` 1), `grep -rn 'section-landed' reckon/` = 5 non-docstring sites, `grep -rn 'c-run-' reckon/` = the two named owners, and `grep -rn '== "implementable"' reckon/` = the six named lines.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `strip_tags` (reckon/_plan_html.py, over the existing `_TAG_RE`), `plan_headings` and the machinery-element predicate each name a distinct consumer that crosses a package boundary, and `structured_section_spans` and `landed_section_ids` are re-expressed rather than forked.
